correctness.rationale: For iid labels with p_i>0 and closed empirical first/last intervals, max first occurrence becomes τ, the final new label arrival time; common intersection at n is equivalent to every other label appearing at least once strictly after τ. This gives pathwise T=τ+second collection suffix, independent of pre-τ data by strong Markov. Inclusion-exclusion for P(τ=t,L=ℓ) and probability all other labels reappear yields the exact arbitrary-p finite-n CDF. Under p_i=1/m the two phases have mutually independent Geom(j/m) waiting times j=1..m and j=1..m−1; exact PGF, mean 2mH_m−1, variance 2m²H_m^(2)−2mH_m, first possible time 2m−1, and sum of two independent standard Gumbel limits by classical coupon-collector with Bonferroni bounds. Independent exhaustive words m=2,3,4 through n=8 and a separate dynamic-programming comparison validate finite cases; do not conflate nonuniform CDF and uniform limit.
residual_risks: Requires stationary independent labels, all p_i>0, and singleton intervals permitted; no dependent or physical-time extension.
Gumbel convergence is weak convergence only; no error rate claimed.
